Shape.Name: Sheet.1597
Shape.Text:
The Host PC is connected to the Gradient chain through the Ethernet Switch. The Gradient information, in turn, passes through the Ethernet Switch to the CAM Chassis via the AGP Board. From the AGP board, information is passed to the SRF/TRF board via the CAM backplane. The SRF/TRF board operates as the brains of the process, passing the signal on to the other two boards via the CAM backplane.
Once fully processed the signal is sent to the Cronus Chassis in the XGD before the Gradient Pulse is generated.

Shape.Text: The signal path for the boards in the CAM Chassis passes through the boards in the following order: 1. Waveform commands originate in the AGP and are passed on to the SRF/TRF. 2. From the SRF/TRF to the IRF3, via the backplane, 3. From the IRF3 to the Cronus Chassis, GMC board. 4,5. The clock signal originates in the Exciter and is passed to the Cronus Chassis GMC board, and CAM IRF3 board for synchronization. 6. Gradient Pulse and clock signals are passed from the GMC to the XGAs for pulse creation.

Shape.Name: Sheet.1619
Shape.Text:
When diagnostics are initiated by the FE, 1. Status/control path originates in the Host, and passes to the Ethernet Switch, then 2. To the SCP. The SCP translates the command and passes it to either the Ethernet Switch or the SRF/TRF board (depending on which diagnostic is requested). 2,3. When a Static Test or Fidelity Diagnostic is requested, the SCP passes the translated command to Cronus Chassis GMC board via the Ethernet Switch, and the GMC board executes the command. 4. When a Gradient Hammer Test is requested, the SCP passes the translated command to the SRF/TRF board, which executes the command.
Real-time diagnostic execution involves the following path: 5. From the SRF/TRF to the IRF3, then 6. To the Cronus Chassis GMC board, then, 7. To the XGA Control Board, via the Cronus backplane, and to the XGAs So if there are multiple failures, the failure in the later steps will not come to light until the failure in the earlier step has been addressed.
